dataset.name: MASSIVE
dataset.citation: FitzGerald et al., MASSIVE: A 1M-Example Multilingual Natural Language Understanding Dataset with 51 Typologically-Diverse Languages, ACL 2023

sampling.note: Per-project overrides below apply when a project's official split cannot supply the standard size. Fallback sizes are the ones named in PROJECT_PLAN.md section 4.

projects.name: Home assistant
projects.rationale: Alarms and connected-home device control are what a single home-assistant product covers. 12 intents, so candidate choice is a real decision and the intent macro-F1 is not dominated by two classes.

projects.name: Productivity assistant
projects.rationale: Calendar, email and list management are the standard scope of a work-productivity assistant. 10 intents and the largest train split, and its longer entity schema makes prompts bigger than P1's, which stresses the prompt-size cap.

projects.name: Ordering and travel
projects.override_reason: The official en-US test split holds only 181 in-scope cases for these two domains, short of the 250 the standard size needs. PROJECT_PLAN.md section 4 names 200 as the test fallback, so P3 uses it: 167 in-scope + 33 out-of-scope. Decided at G2 from split counts alone, before any prediction and before any P3 content was inspected.
projects.rationale: Ordering food and arranging travel is a coherent transactional assistant, and it is deliberately unlike P1 and P2 in purpose, so adaptation to it is a real generalisation test.

oos_pool.rule: Out-of-scope cases for every project come only from these reserved domains, which no project uses. Cases are sampled disjointly across projects, so no utterance serves as out-of-scope evidence for more than one project.
oos_pool.note: No system is trained on out-of-scope examples. Out-of-scope thresholds are tuned on development data only.
